title: Tangled
description: "Use Tangled, a forge built on atproto: issues, pulls, comments, live events and webhooks."
icon: i-lucide-spool

The Tangled provider covers [Tangled](https://tangled.org), a forge built on atproto. It reads and writes issues, pulls and comments. It also streams live events from Jetstream and verifies incoming push webhooks. Tangled has no reviews, checks, releases or repository contents API, so those capabilities are `false`.

## Authentication

Reads are public and need no credentials. Writes need an atproto session, from an app password or from an OAuth client:

```ts
import { tangled } from 'forges/tangled'

const reader = tangled({}).create()

const writer = tangled({
  auth: {
    type: 'app_password',
    identifier: 'alice.example.com',
    password: process.env.TANGLED_APP_PASSWORD!,
  },
}).create()
```

With `app_password`, the provider creates a session on the account's PDS (personal data server). It finds the PDS in this order:

1. The `pds` option, if you pass it.
2. The DID document, if `identifier` is a DID.
3. `https://bsky.social`.

With `oauth`, pass the `did`, the `pds` and a `fetch` from an atproto OAuth client that signs requests:

```ts
tangled({
  auth: {
    type: 'oauth',
    did: session.did,
    pds: session.pds,
    fetch: session.fetch,
  },
})
```

## Instance and services

`baseUrl` defaults to `https://tangled.org`. The provider uses it for web links and as the instance.

Tangled records are stored on many servers, so the provider reads from several services. You can change each one:

| Option | Reads | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plcUrl` | DID documents, to find each author's PDS | `https://plc.directory` |
| `backlinksUrl` | Records that point at a thread, such as comments | `https://constellation.microcosm.blue` |
| `handleResolverUrl` | The DID for a handle, when a ref's `owner` is a handle | `https://public.api.bsky.app` |
| `recordsUrl` | Records, through a Slingshot-compatible cache | Each author's PDS |
| `jetstreamUrl` | The live event stream | A public Bluesky Jetstream instance |
| `apiUrl` | `request()` and `listSource: 'index'` | `https://api.tangled.org` |

## Refs and numbers

Issues and pulls are atproto records, identified by AT-URI. A `ThreadRef` has the AT-URI as both `number` and `externalId`. The repo's `owner` is the owner's DID, and `RepoRef.externalId` is the repo DID.

A repo's `name` in the refs the provider returns is the key of its repo record. For newer repos, that key differs from the name people see, which `Repo.displayName` holds. You can pass a ref with a handle as `owner` and the visible name as `name`, as `parseUrl()` returns for a URL such as `https://tangled.org/@acme.example.com/widgets`. The provider resolves the handle and finds the record by name, so the ref it returns may differ from the one you passed.

The numbers in the Tangled UI and in webhooks come from the appview, and records don't store them. The provider reports them as `displayNumber`.

A ref from a webhook has no `number` until it's matched to a record. To fill `number` during `webhooks.ingest()`, pass a `resolveDisplayNumber(repo, kind, displayNumber)` function that returns the AT-URI.

## Thread state

A thread's state is the latest state record written by the thread's author, the repo owner or a collaborator. The provider ignores state records from other accounts. If another account calls `close()` or `reopen()`, the call throws `InsufficientScopeError` and writes no record.

## Listing threads

By default, `threads.list()` reads every record and computes each thread's state, which takes several requests per thread. Set `listSource: 'index'` to list from the index at `apiUrl`. The index takes one request per page, but its states can lag behind the records. Every listing from the index has an `index_possibly_stale` warning.

## Notifications

Notifications use the `org.tangled.temp.notification.*` lexicons. These lexicons are in Tangled's temporary namespace and can change. To enable notifications, pass `auth` and set `notificationsUrl` to the base URL of the notification service. The notification capabilities are then `'experimental'`.

Stars and follows have no thread. They appear with `kind: 'other'`, and `typeRaw` contains the notification type.

## Merging

The knot that hosts a repository merges its pulls, with no review step. `merge()` and `approveAndMerge()` are unavailable.

## Live events

`sources.subscribe()` streams events from Jetstream. Each item has a `cursor`. Save it, and pass it back to resume the stream:

```ts
for await (const { event, cursor } of reader.sources.subscribe({
  cursor: saved,
  signal,
})) {
  console.log(event.kind, event.summary)
  saved = cursor
}
```

To close the connection, abort the signal or break out of the loop. If the connection drops, the iterator throws `SubscriptionClosedError` with the last cursor. The provider doesn't reconnect, so call `subscribe()` again with that cursor.

## Webhooks

Set `webhookSecret` to the secret configured on the hook:

```ts
const forge = tangled({
  webhookSecret: process.env.TANGLED_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
}).create()

const events = await forge.webhooks.ingest({
  headers: request.headers,
  body: await request.text(),
})
```

Tangled sends these headers with each delivery:

| Header | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `X-Tangled-Signature-256` | `sha256=` followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body |
| `X-Tangled-Event` | The event name |
| `X-Tangled-Delivery` | The delivery ID |

A `push` delivery becomes a `push` or `ref` event. Tangled has no API to register hooks, so the `webhooks` management methods are unavailable.

::contributing{title="Record Tangled fixtures" to="/contributing/record-fixtures"}
Recording needs no credentials:

```sh
pnpm record-fixtures tangled
```

To record other threads, set `FIXTURE_TANGLED_ISSUE` and `FIXTURE_TANGLED_PULL` to AT-URIs. To record through a Slingshot cache, set `TANGLED_RECORDS_URL`.
::
